target.title: fix(heartbeat): skip plugin bootstrap and bundled fallback during delivery target resolution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a heartbeat wake-loop latency regression where delivery-target resolution blocks for ~60s per tick when the configured channel plugin is not already in the active runtime registry.

### Background

Commit [`6470bb7625`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6470bb7625) ("fix(heartbeat): bootstrap plugin session targets, #93630") solved a real problem: when a user configured `heartbeat.target` to a channel id not in the built-in known-deliverable-channel list, `normalizeDeliverableOutboundChannel()` returned `undefined` and the target was silently dropped to `"none"`.

The fix called `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin({ allowBootstrap: true })` in the heartbeat delivery-target path. However, this triggers `resolveRuntimePluginRegistry()` → `loadOpenClawPlugins()`, which scans **all** installed plugins — not just the target channel.

### Root cause

The `bootstrapAttempts` guard in `channel-bootstrap.runtime.ts` caches per `(registryVersion, channel)` key:
- **Successful bootstrap**: key stays cached → subsequent ticks skip instantly
- **Failed bootstrap** (plugin not installed / config issue): key is deleted → every tick re-runs the full scan

This is the pathological case: a misconfigured or not-yet-installed heartbeat plugin channel causes repeated scans on every wake tick.

### Trigger conditions

1. `heartbeat.target` is not `"none"` or `"last"`
2. The target channel is not in the active runtime registry
3. `heartbeat.to` is set (non-empty)

## Changes

### Part 1: Hot path optimization

Three heartbeat-path call sites in `targets.ts` now pass `allowBootstrap: false, allowBundledFallback: false`. A new `allowBundledFallback` parameter (default `true`) in `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin` lets hot paths skip both bootstrap and `getBundledChannelPlugin` lazy-load.

### Part 2: Startup pre-activation

`preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins()` in `heartbeat-pre-activate.ts` runs once at gateway startup (in `activateGatewayScheduledServices`, before `startHeartbeatRunner`). It finds every non-standard heartbeat channel target and calls `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin({ allowBootstrap: true })` to load plugins into the active registry before the wake loop starts.

This preserves the delivery compatibility from #93630 while moving bootstrap cost from every tick to startup (once).

### Part 3: Per-agent heartbeat coverage (rev 2)

Pre-activation iterates both `agents.defaults.heartbeat` AND `agents.list[].heartbeat` entries, merging per-agent overrides over defaults (matching `resolveHeartbeatConfig` in the runner). Per-agent external plugin targets — which the runner schedules independently — are also pre-activated.

## User Impact

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Plugin active in registry | <10ms (same) | <10ms (same) |
| Plugin not active (external, per-agent) | ~60s every tick | ~629ms once at startup, then <2ms |
| Plugin not installed | ~60s every tick | fast fail (<10ms) |
| Standard channel (telegram, qqbot) | <10ms (same) | <10ms (same, pre-activation no-op) |

## Compatibility

- `allowBundledFallback` defaults to `true` — all non-heartbeat callers unchanged
- Pre-activation is a no-op for standard channels and `target: none/last`
- Per-agent `agents.list[].heartbeat` targets covered with same merge semantics as the runner
- `resolveOutboundTarget` continues to pass `params.allowBootstrap` transparently

## Evidence

### Unit tests (96/96 passed)

```
src/infra/outbound/targets.test.ts                  85 passed
src/infra/outbound/heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts   11 passed
```

### Real behavior proof (reproducible: `npx vitest run`)

```
[PROOF] pre-activate qqbot (standard):               1ms   ← standard channel no-op
[PROOF] pre-activate external-channel (bootstrap):  629ms   ← one-time startup bootstrap
[PROOF] pre-activate per-agent external-channel:    107ms   ← per-agent target covered
[PROOF] hot-path tick 1: channel=external-channel to=resolved in 2ms   ← no bootstrap
[PROOF] hot-path tick 2: channel=external-channel to=resolved in 1ms
[PROOF] hot-path tick 3: channel=external-channel to=resolved in 0ms
[PROOF] hot-path tick 4: channel=external-channel to=resolved in 0ms
[PROOF] hot-path tick 5: channel=external-channel to=resolved in 1ms
[PROOF] resolveOutboundChannelPlugin allowBootstrap=true:  0ms → ext
[PROOF] resolveOutboundChannelPlugin allowBootstrap=false: 0ms → ext
[PROOF] Same result: YES                                     ← preserved delivery
[PROOF] session-route resolution: channel=ext to=t in 3ms   ← hot path, no bootstrap
```

**Proof demonstrates**: (1) startup pre-activation resolves external plugins once, (2) every subsequent hot-path tick resolves instantly with no bootstrap, (3) channel and target are correctly delivered (not dropped), (4) per-agent heartbeat targets are covered.

### Lint / type / format / build

```
oxlint:    clean
tsgo:      clean (check:test-types)
format:    clean (oxfmt --check)
build:     clean (pnpm build)
```

### Review response history

- **ClawSweeper rev 1** (sha `9d5e814eb8`): Disabled bootstrap on hot path only → reviewer flagged missing delivery compatibility for external plugins. Added startup pre-activation.
- **ClawSweeper rev 2** (sha `310aaf3ddb`): Added pre-activation but only covered defaults → reviewer flagged missing per-agent coverage. Extended to iterate `agents.list[].heartbeat`.
- **Current** (sha `f3156912ea`): Pre-activation covers both defaults and per-agent overrides, with reproducible proof of startup activation, fast wake resolution, and preserved delivery.
